blocks.task_summary: Find the unknown frequency x in a grouped frequency table given that the median is 4.5 hours.
method_path: Recognise that median = 4.5 implies total frequency n = 20 and half the total frequency is 10
Set up cumulative frequency: 5+1+4 = 10 values ≤ 4 hours
accepted_alternatives: Set up 5+1+4 = 3+x and solve to obtain x = 7
State Σf = 20 and solve 13+x = 20 to obtain x = 7

evidence.basis: EITHER: recognising that half the total frequency is 10 (A1). OR: 5+1+4 = 3+x (A1). OR: Σf = 20 (A1). THEN: x = 7 (A1).

blocks.task_summary: Find the standard deviation of the exercising times.
method_path: Calculate variance: σ² = Σf(x-μ)²/Σf = 2.51 or σ² = Σfx²/Σf - μ² = 2.51
accepted_alternatives: Manual using σ² = Σfx²/n - μ² = 2.51 → σ = 1.58

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: 1.58429... 1.58 A2. METHOD 2: variance formula with (A1) for correct setup, then σ = 1.58429... = 1.58 A1.

blocks.task_summary: Find the area of one shaded circular segment in terms of θ, given radius 2 cm and angle θ.
method_path: Area of segment = area of sector − area of triangle

evidence.basis: valid approach to find area of segment by finding area of sector – area of triangle (M1); ½r²θ − ½r²sinθ; ½(2)²θ − ½(2)²sinθ (A1); area = 2θ − 2sinθ A1

blocks.task_summary: Given logo area = 13.4 cm², formed by removing two equal segments from a 5×4 cm rectangle, find θ using GDC.
accepted_alternatives: Find area of one segment = (20 − 13.4)/2 = 3.3, solve 2θ − 2sinθ = 3.3 using GDC, θ = 2.36

evidence.basis: EITHER area of logo = area of rectangle – area of segments (M1); 5×4 − 2×(2θ−2sinθ) = 13.4 (A1); OR area of one segment = (20−13.4)/2 = 3.3 (M1); 2θ−2sinθ = 3.3 (A1); THEN θ = 2.35672...; θ = 2.36 (do not accept an answer in degrees) A1

blocks.task_summary: Show that setting the sum of probabilities to 1 yields 2k^2 - k + 0.12 = 0.
Solve the quadratic for k, reject k = 0.2 because it makes P(X=1) negative, and give k = 0.3.
method_path: Solve 2k^2 - k + 0.12 = 0 to obtain k = 0.2 or k = 0.3
Note that P(X=1) = k - 0.28 must be nonnegative
Reject k = 0.2 because it gives P(X=1) < 0

evidence.basis: one of 0.2 OR 0.3 (M1) ... k = 0.3 A1 ... reasoning to reject k = 0.2 eg P(1) = k - 0.28 >= 0 therefore k != 0.2 R1

blocks.task_summary: Use E(X) = sum x * P(X=x) with k = 0.3 to obtain E(X) = 1.27.

evidence.basis: attempting to use the expected value formula (M1) ... = 1.27 A1

blocks.task_summary: Find the time t when the particle is at rest by solving v(t) = e^(sin t) + 4 sin t = 0 for t in [0, 6].
method_path: Solve e^(sin t) + 4 sin t = 0 using GDC

evidence.basis: recognizing at rest v=0 (M1); t = 3.34692... t = 3.35 (seconds) A1; Note: Award (M1)A0 for any other solution to v=0 eg t=-0.205 or t=6.08.

blocks.task_summary: Find the acceleration when the particle changes direction by differentiating v(t) and evaluating a(t) at the t from part (a).
method_path: Recognize direction change occurs when v = 0 at t = 3.34692...
Differentiate v(t): a(t) = e^(sin t) cos t + 4 cos t

evidence.basis: recognizing particle changes direction when v=0 OR when t=3.34692... (M1); a = -4.71439... a = -4.71 (ms^-2) A2

blocks.task_summary: Find the total distance travelled by integrating the absolute value of v(t) from t = 0 to 6.
method_path: Set total distance = integral of |v(t)| from 0 to 6
Split at t = 3.34692... where v changes sign
Evaluate integral of v(t) from 0 to 3.34692... plus integral of -v(t) from 3.34692... to 6 using GDC
accepted_alternatives: Direct evaluation of integral of |v(t)| from 0 to 6 using GDC without explicit splitting

evidence.basis: distance travelled = integral_0^6 |v| dt OR split integrals (A1); = 20.7534... = 20.8 (metres) A1

blocks.task_summary: Given independent A, B with P(A∩B′)=0.16 and P(A′∩B)=0.36, let P(A∩B)=x and find x.
accepted_alternatives: Form equations P(A)(1−P(B))=0.16 and (1−P(A))P(B)=0.36 using independence, solve simultaneously to get P(A)=0.4, P(B)=0.6, then x=P(A)P(B)=0.24

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: one of P(A)=x+0.16 OR P(B)=x+0.36 (A1); attempt to equate P(A∩B) with P(A)×P(B) (M1); x=(0.16+x)(0.36+x) (A1); x=0.24 (A1). METHOD 2: attempt to form at least one equation in P(A) and P(B) using independence (M1); P(A)=0.4 AND P(B)=0.6 (A1); P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B)=0.4×0.6=0.24 (A1); x=0.24 (A1).

blocks.task_summary: Find P(A′|B′) using the result x=0.24 from part (a).
method_path: Recognise P(A′|B′)=P(A′) by independence of complements

blocks.task_summary: Show that f(x) = 1/(2^x) - 2^x is an odd function.
method_path: Show f(-x) = -f(x) and conclude f is odd
accepted_alternatives: Graphical approach: show graph is invariant under 180 degree rotation about origin, or invariant under reflection in y-axis then x-axis (earns M1A0 per markscheme)

evidence.basis: attempt to replace x with -x M1
EITHER f(-x) = (1-2^(-x))/2^(-x) = -(1-2^x)/2^x = -f(x) OR equivalent simplification A1
so f is an odd function AG

Note: Award M1A0 for a graphical approach including evidence that either the graph is invariant after rotation by 180 degrees about the origin or the graph is invariant after a reflection in the y-axis and then in the x-axis (or vice versa).

blocks.task_summary: Solve the inequality f(x) >= g(x) where f(x) = 2^(-x) - 2^x and g(x) = (x-1)/(x^2-2x-3), with x not equal to -1, 3.

blocks.task_summary: Find the possible range of values for |a + b| given a = (12, −5) and |b| = 15.

evidence.basis: |a| = √(12²+(−5)²) = 13 (A1); 2 ≤ |a+b| ≤ 28 (accept min 2 and max 28) A1. Note: Award (A1)A0 for 2 and 28 seen with no indication that they are the endpoints of an interval.

blocks.task_summary: Given that |a + b| is a minimum, find vector p = a + b.
method_path: recognise that for minimum |a + b|, b is antiparallel to a

evidence.basis: recognition that p or b is a negative multiple of a (M1); p = −(2/13)a OR b = (15/13)(−12, 5) and p = (−12/13, 5/13)×2 (A1)

blocks.task_summary: Find q = (x, y) with x, y ∈ ℝ⁺ such that |q| = 15 and q is perpendicular to a = (12, −5).
method_path: q ⟂ a ⇒ direction of q is (5, 12)
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: set scalar product q·a = 0 ⇒ 12x − 5y = 0; solve simultaneously with x² + y² = 225 to obtain q = (75/13, 180/13)

evidence.basis: METHOD 2: attempt to set scalar product q·a = 0 OR product of gradients = −1 (M1); 12x − 5y = 0 (A1); |q| = √(x²+y²) = 15; attempt to solve simultaneously to find a quadratic in x or in y (M1); q = (75/13, 180/13) (A1A1). Note: Award A1 independently for each value.

blocks.task_summary: Write down an expression for the product of the roots of kx^2 - (k+3)x + 2k+9 = 0 in terms of k.
method_path: Apply Vieta: product of roots = c/a = (2k+9)/k

evidence.basis: product of roots = (2k+9)/k A1 [1 mark]

blocks.task_summary: Determine the values of k such that the equation kx^2 - (k+3)x + 2k+9 = 0 has one positive and one negative real root.
method_path: Recognise one positive and one negative root implies product of roots < 0
Find critical values k = -9/2 and k = 0

evidence.basis: recognition that the product of the roots will be negative (M1); (2k+9)/k < 0; critical values k = 0, -9/2 seen (A1); -9/2 < k < 0 A1 [3 marks]

blocks.task_summary: Find the number of ways 5 people can be seated next to each other in a row of 10 empty seats.
method_path: Treat the 5 people as a contiguous block
Count block positions: 10 minus 5 plus 1 equals 6

evidence.basis: 6 times 5! (A1)(A1) equals 720 (accept 6!) A1

blocks.task_summary: Find the number of ways 4 girls and Peter can be seated in 10 seats such that no girl sits adjacent to Peter; girls need not sit together.
method_path: Identify two cases: Peter at an end vs Peter not at an end
Case 1 (Peter at either end): 2 times 8P4 equals 3360
Case 2 (Peter not at end): 8 times 7P4 equals 6720
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2 complement: 10P5 minus arrangements where Peter adjacent to at least one girl. Case 1: Peter at end next to girl gives 2 times 4 times 8P3 equals 2688. Case 2: Peter not at end gives 8 times 2 times 4 times 7P3 plus 8 times 4 times 3 times 7P2 equals 17472. Total: 10P5 minus (2688 plus 17472) equals 10080.
Combination-based: case 1 as 8C4 times 2 times 4! equals 3360; case 2 as 7C4 times 8 times 4! equals 6720

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: case 1 Peter at either end 8P4x2=3360 OR 8C4x2x4!=3360 (A1); case 2 Peter not at end 7P4x8=6720 (A1); Total=3360+6720=10080 A1
METHOD 2: case 1 Peter at end 8P3x2x4=2688 (A1); case 2 Peter not at end (7P3x8x2x4)+(7P2x4x3)=17472 (A1); Total=10P5-(2688+17472)=10080 A1

blocks.task_summary: Use the substitution y=vx to transform dy/dx=(y²-2x²)/x² into the separable DE x dv/dx = v²-v-2.
method_path: Set y = vx and differentiate: dy/dx = v + x dv/dx
Substitute y=vx and dy/dx=v+x dv/dx into dy/dx = (y²-2x²)/x²
Simplify: v + x dv/dx = v² - 2 → x dv/dx = v² - v - 2 (AG)

evidence.basis: y = vx ⇒ dy/dx = v + x dv/dx (A1); replacing y with vx and dy/dx with v + x dv/dx (M1); v + x dv/dx = v² - 2 (A1) leading to x dv/dx = v² - v - 2 AG

blocks.task_summary: Solve the separable DE via partial fractions to obtain the exact solution, evaluate at x=1.5, and interpret the poor Euler approximation using gradient behaviour or the vertical asymptote.
method_path: Integrate both sides: (1/3)(ln|v-2| - ln|v+1|) = ln|x| + c
Use initial condition v=3 at x=1 to find c = (1/3)ln(1/4) or A = 1/4
Combine logarithms to ln|(v-2)/(v+1)| = ln|(1/4)x³| or equivalent
Substitute v=y/x and solve for y to obtain y = (4x³+8x)/(4-x³)
Explain poor Euler estimate: gradient changes rapidly on [1, 1.5] / vertical asymptote at x = ∛4 ≈ 1.5874
accepted_alternatives: Constant of integration found via c = (1/3)ln(1/4) and single-logarithm combination, or via combined-logarithm constant A = 1/4 (both accepted in markscheme).

evidence.basis: (c)(i) attempt to separate variables (M1); dv/(v²-v-2) = dx/x (A1); attempt partial fractions (M1); 1/((v-2)(v+1)) = (1/3)(1/(v-2)-1/(v+1)) (A1); (1/3)(ln|v-2|-ln|v+1|)=ln x + c (A1); attempt to find c (M1); single logarithm (M1)
EITHER/OR routes for constant; substitute v=y/x (M1); attempt to make y the subject (M1); y=(4x³+8x)/(4-x³) (A1)
(c)(ii) actual y at x=1.5 is 27.3 (A1); (c)(iii) gradient changes rapidly / vertical asymptote at x=∛4≈1.5874... (R1)
